description: A high-performance inference engine for AI models

summary.one_liner: A Rust inference engine for running AI models locally in apps, with bindings for Swift, Python and TypeScript, aimed mainly at Apple devices via Metal.
summary.what_it_does: uzu is a native Rust crate for running AI models on-device, with bindings exposed for Swift (uniffi-rs), Python (pyo3) and TypeScript (napi-rs). The README describes an Engine API that downloads a model, opens a chat session, and returns replies, with streaming replies also supported. It supports chat with a shared loaded model instance, structured output via a JSON schema grammar, and external tool calls. It also includes cloud model usage (an OpenAI API key example is shown). A CLI can browse, download and chat with models, run benchmarks, and serve an OpenAI-compatible HTTP endpoint (/v1/chat/completions and /v1/models). Backends listed are metal, webgpu and cpu. A model format conversion path via the separate lalamo tool is mentioned.
use_cases: run an LLM locally inside a mobile or desktop app
private on-device chat without inference costs
structured JSON output from a local model
tool/function calling with a local model
serve a local OpenAI-compatible chat API
text-to-speech or model inference on Apple devices
how_to_run: Add the Rust crate: uzu = { git = "...", branch = "main", package = "uzu" } (or uv add uzu==0.6.13 for Python, pnpm add @trymirai/uzu@0.6.13 for TypeScript)
notable: Single high-level Engine API shared across Rust, Swift, Python and TypeScript
OpenAI-compatible HTTP server mode from the CLI
Uses unified memory on Apple devices
Structured output via JSON schema grammar
Traceable computations for checking correctness against reference implementations
caveats: Several targets (Windows, Linux, WebAssembly) are marked as in progress in the README
Each model may use a significant amount of RAM; the README recommends keeping one session loaded at a time
iOS apps are advised to add the Increased Memory Capability entitlement
